page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-384 provides an extensive compute environment based on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 384 dedicated vCPUs and 3024 GB of system memory. The resulting ratio of approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU makes it suitable for execution profiles that require substantial memory capacity alongside parallel thread scalability.

Hardware configuration on this instance is strictly centered on centralized processor and memory scaling. It contains zero GPUs, directing all platform resources to standard compute tasks. Bundled local storage is not provided, meaning the instance relies entirely on external network-attached block storage for system images, persistent files, and scratch space.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, consolidating 384 dedicated vCPUs and over three terabytes of memory within a single instance eliminates the network latency and distributed state management overhead associated with horizontal multi-node clusters. A primary operational consideration is managing storage throughput, as all input and output demands must traverse the network fabric due to the lack of on-chassis drives.

This server matches workloads that maintain expansive working datasets in active memory while consuming large thread pools. Representative applications include massive in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning platforms, real-time analytics processing, memory-intensive caching clusters, and high-volume ETL data pipelines.

This configuration fits high-throughput transactional database systems, massive in-memory caching layers, enterprise resource planning installations, large data pipelines, and distributed analytics processing tasks.
